spindle_specs.warmup_procedure: Main spindle: S200 for 5 min, S500 for 5 min, S1500 for 5 min, S3000 for 5 min, S5000 for 5 min. Milling spindle: S500 for 5 min, S2000 for 5 min, S5000 for 5 min, S8000 for 5 min, S12000 for 5 min. Both required after >4 hrs idle.

axes.name: X
axes.notes: Cross-slide axis. Used for turning diameter and milling Y-equivalent when B=90.

axes.name: Y
axes.notes: Milling head offset axis. Allows off-center milling, cross-drilling, and Y-axis contouring.

axes.name: B
axes.notes: Milling spindle tilt axis. B=0 is spindle parallel to Z. B=90 is spindle perpendicular to Z (standard milling).

axes.name: C
axes.notes: Main spindle C-axis for indexing and contouring. Full 360-degree continuous for polar interpolation and cylindrical interpolation.

Constant RPM mode. Required for threading and milling operations.

Cylindrical interpolation. Maps flat XY toolpath onto cylindrical surface for engraving, keyways, and spline cutting on OD/ID surfaces.
Coordinate system rotation. Rotates XY plane by specified angle for angled feature machining.
Tilted working plane for 3+2 machining. Defines inclined coordinate system using Euler angles combined with B-axis positioning.

Milling spindle forward (CW). Activates the B-axis milling spindle.
Through-spindle coolant ON (milling spindle). Activates HSK-A63 through-spindle coolant.
B-axis clamp. Locks the B-axis for 3+2 milling operations.
B-axis unclamp. Releases B-axis for positioning.
Program end and rewind / Subprogram return.

probing_cycles.description: Skip cutting / probe touch signal. Moves axis until probe triggers.
Automatic tool length measurement via tool setter.

alarm_codes.description: Program format error. Illegal character or invalid syntax in NC program block.
corrective_actions: Verify G/M code is valid for OSP-P300S

alarm_codes.description: G-code group conflict. Two G-codes from the same modal group in one block.
probable_causes: Conflicting modal codes in same block
Post processor error mixing turning and milling modal groups
corrective_actions: Split conflicting G-codes into separate blocks
Verify post processor handles mill-turn modal switching correctly

alarm_codes.description: Travel limit exceeded. Commanded position exceeds soft limit for an axis.
probable_causes: B-axis angle causes tool path to exceed X/Y/Z limits
corrective_actions: Verify coordinates against travel limits (X:630 Y:230 Z:820)
Verify B-axis angle does not extend tool beyond envelope

alarm_codes.description: Mill-turn spindle synchronization error. Main spindle and milling spindle RPM mismatch during synchronized operation.
probable_causes: Spindle encoder fault on either spindle
Excessive cutting load causing main spindle speed variation
M200 sync command while spindles at different speeds
corrective_actions: Cancel synchronization with M201 and restart at matched speeds
Reduce cutting load during synchronized operations
Verify synchronization parameters in CNC diagnostic screen

alarm_codes.description: Mill-turn mode switching error. Failure transitioning between turning mode and milling mode.
probable_causes: B-axis not at valid milling position (B=90) before milling mode command
C-axis not engaged before polar interpolation
Turret tool active when milling spindle operation commanded
corrective_actions: Verify B-axis is at commanded angle before switching to milling mode
Ensure correct spindle (main vs milling) is selected for the operation

alarm_codes.description: Dual-spindle clash detection. Anti-collision system detected potential interference between turret and milling head.
probable_causes: Simultaneous X/Z move brings turret and milling head into conflict zone
B-axis angle extends milling tool into turret work zone
Tool length offset error creates interference condition
corrective_actions: Machine will stop all axes — do NOT jog without verifying clearance
Check tool offsets for both turret and milling spindle tools
Review program for proper turret retract before milling head approach
Enable collision avoidance checking (M310) at mode transitions

alarm_codes.description: B-axis overtravel. B-axis position exceeded -30 or +210 degree limits.
probable_causes: Program commanded B-axis angle beyond travel range
Post processor not clamping B-axis output to -30 to +210 range
corrective_actions: Verify B-axis command is within -30 to +210 degrees
Fix post processor B-axis angle limits
Check B-axis encoder connection if alarm occurs at legal angles

alarm_codes.description: B-axis servo error. Following error on B-axis exceeded threshold during positioning.
probable_causes: B-axis clamp (M68) still engaged during positioning command
Roller gear cam mechanism needs lubrication
B-axis servo motor overload from heavy tool assembly
corrective_actions: Verify M69 (B-axis unclamp) is called before B-axis move
Verify tool assembly weight does not exceed milling head capacity

alarm_codes.description: Y-axis overtravel. Y-axis position exceeded +/-115mm travel limits.
probable_causes: Y-axis activated without proper G-code context
Post processor not accounting for Y-axis travel on MULTUS
corrective_actions: Verify Y-axis commands are within +/-115mm range
Ensure Y-axis is activated only for milling operations
Check post processor Y-axis output limits

alarm_codes.description: Y-axis milling error. Y-axis feed commanded during turning mode.
probable_causes: Y-axis move programmed while machine is in turning mode (milling spindle not active)
Post processor outputting Y moves without mode switch to milling
Y-axis not zeroed before switching from milling to turning mode
corrective_actions: Switch to milling mode before commanding Y-axis moves
Return Y-axis to zero before switching to turning mode
Verify post processor inserts proper mode switch codes

alarm_codes.description: Main spindle motor overheat. Main turning spindle winding temperature exceeded thermal limit.
probable_causes: Sustained heavy turning at high torque
corrective_actions: Stop machine and allow 30 min cooldown

alarm_codes.description: Milling spindle motor overheat. B-axis milling spindle winding temperature exceeded limit.
probable_causes: Extended heavy milling without coolant breaks
Through-spindle coolant not activated for deep pocketing
corrective_actions: Stop milling spindle and allow cooldown
Activate through-spindle coolant (M50) for heavy milling

alarm_codes.description: X-axis servo error excessive. Following error exceeded alarm threshold.
Main spindle drive fault. Main spindle servo amplifier internal error.
Milling spindle drive fault. Milling spindle servo amplifier internal error.
ATC tool change error. Milling spindle ATC failed to complete tool exchange.
corrective_actions: Check ATC arm position via diagnostic screen
Clean HSK taper face and tool holder
Verify tool dimensions against ATC clearance

alarm_codes.description: ATC magazine rotation error. Milling tool magazine failed to index to commanded pocket.
probable_causes: Tool protrusion beyond maximum gauge length
corrective_actions: Verify tool lengths do not exceed 350mm
Run magazine test in maintenance mode

alarm_codes.description: Chuck pressure low. Hydraulic chuck clamping pressure below safe operating minimum.
Turret index error. Lower turret failed to complete rotation to commanded station.
Way lube oil level low. Centralized lubrication reservoir below minimum.
Main power supply voltage abnormal.

maintenance_schedule.task: Check and refill way lube reservoir
procedure_steps: Check way lube reservoir level via sight glass
Refill with ISO VG68 if below LOW mark
Check for leaks under machine

parts_needed.description: Way lube oil ISO VG68 (20L pail)

maintenance_schedule.task: Check hydraulic oil level and chuck/tailstock pressure
procedure_steps: Check hydraulic reservoir sight glass
Verify chuck pressure 25-40 bar
Cycle chuck open/close
Check tailstock pressure 20-35 bar
safety_warnings: Never operate with chuck pressure below 20 bar

procedure_steps: Run main spindle warmup: S200>S500>S1500>S3000>S5000, 5 min each
Run milling spindle warmup: S500>S2000>S5000>S8000>S12000, 5 min each
Monitor bearing temperatures on diagnostic screen
Both should stabilize within ambient + 15 deg C
safety_warnings: Ensure chuck is empty and ATC has no tool during warmup

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean chip pan and chip conveyor
procedure_steps: Empty chip tray
Clear chips from turret base and B-axis head area
Check conveyor belt operation
Clean coolant strainer basket
safety_warnings: Verify both spindles stopped before reaching into work area

procedure_steps: Measure concentration with refractometer (target 6-10%)
Measure pH (target 8.5-9.5)
Skim tramp oil if pH < 8.0
Record readings
Remove and blow clean both cabinet filters
Inspect for tears — replace if damaged
Verify both cabinet fans running
safety_warnings: Do not open cabinet interior — high voltage

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean and inspect HSK-A63 taper on milling spindle
procedure_steps: Remove tool from milling spindle
Clean HSK taper bore with lint-free cloth
Inspect taper face for nicks, scratches, or coolant residue
Clean face contact surface — HSK depends on face + taper contact
Apply light film of spindle oil to taper
Verify drawbar pull force with HSK test arbor
safety_warnings: HSK requires both face and taper contact — any contamination degrades rigidity

procedure_steps: Put B-axis in maintenance mode
Index B-axis through full range (-30 to +210)
Listen for abnormal noise or vibration during rotation
Check B-axis clamp torque via diagnostic screen
Verify 0.001-degree positioning accuracy with precision level
safety_warnings: Keep hands clear of B-axis during motion — high clamping force

procedure_steps: Index turret through all 12 stations
Verify clamp confirm at each station
Time index — should be within spec
Clean curvic coupling if any station slow or fails
safety_warnings: Keep hands clear during turret indexing

maintenance_schedule.task: Replace coolant filter and skim tramp oil
procedure_steps: Turn off coolant pump
Skim tramp oil
Replace filter cartridge
Check concentration
Restart pump

maintenance_schedule.task: Check axis backlash compensation — all 5 axes
procedure_steps: Measure X/Y/Z backlash with dial indicator method
Measure B-axis backlash with precision level
Measure C-axis backlash with rotary encoder test
Compare all values to stored compensation
Adjust if deviation > 2 um (linear) or 0.002 deg (rotary)
Depressurize system
Drain hydraulic oil
Replace filter element
Refill with ISO VG32
Bleed air
Cycle chuck and tailstock to circulate
safety_warnings: Dispose used oil per local regulations

procedure_steps: Warm up machine for 2 hours
Measure X/Y/Z linear accuracy with laser interferometer
Measure B-axis angular accuracy with rotary calibrator
Measure C-axis angular accuracy
Check B-axis center-of-rotation alignment to spindle centerline
Update compensation tables as needed
Generate calibration certificate

programming_tips.topic: Simultaneous Turning and Milling — Mode Switching Protocol
programming_tips.code_example:
(TURNING OPERATION)
G96 S200 M03 (Main spindle CSS)
G01 X50. Z-30. F0.25
M05 (Stop main spindle)

(SWITCH TO MILLING)
M19 (C-axis engage)
G00 B90. (Milling spindle perpendicular)
M68 (B-axis clamp)
T0101 (Select ATC milling tool)
G97 S5000 M33 (Milling spindle ON)
G01 X25. Y10. Z-5. F800
programming_tips.description: The MULTUS B300II switches between turning and milling by changing which spindle is active and how axes are interpreted. Main spindle (M03/M04/M05) is for turning. Milling spindle (M33/M34/M35) is for milling. C-axis must be engaged (M19) before milling. B-axis must be positioned and clamped (M68) for 3+2 milling. Never command Y-axis moves while in turning mode.
gotchas: Always stop main spindle (M05) before engaging C-axis (M19)
Y-axis must return to Y0. before switching back to turning mode
B-axis clamp (M68) is mandatory for rigid milling — unclamped B produces chatter
Tool offset groups are separate for turret (turning) and ATC (milling) tools

programming_tips.topic: B-Axis Angular Approach for Undercuts and Complex Features
programming_tips.code_example:
G00 B30. (Tilt milling spindle 30 degrees from Z)
M68 (Clamp B-axis)
G97 S8000 M33
G43.4 H1 (TCP ON)
G01 X25. Y0. Z-10. F500
...
G49 (TCP OFF)
M35 (Milling spindle stop)
M69 (B-axis unclamp)
programming_tips.description: The B-axis allows the milling spindle to approach the workpiece at any angle from -30 to +210 degrees. B=0 is the spindle parallel to Z (boring orientation). B=90 is perpendicular to Z (standard cross-milling). B=30 or B=60 enables undercut machining impossible on a standard lathe. TCP (G43.4) must be active to maintain correct tool tip position during angled milling.
gotchas: TCP (G43.4) is mandatory when B is not 0 or 90 — without it, the tool path will be wrong
B-axis clamping (M68) is required for cutting rigidity — do not cut with B unclamped
Tool length offset must be measured at B=0 reference position
Some B-angles reduce effective Y-axis travel — verify clearance at extreme B angles

programming_tips.topic: Y-Axis Offset Limitations and Best Practices
programming_tips.code_example:
G00 B90. (Standard milling position)
M68
G97 S6000 M33
G00 Y0. (Verify Y at center)
G01 Y-15. F500 (Off-center by 15mm — within Y range)
...
G00 Y0. (Return to center before mode switch)
M35
M69
programming_tips.description: The Y-axis on the MULTUS B300II has limited travel (+/-115mm) compared to a full VMC. It provides off-center milling capability for features like cross-holes, flats, and keyways that are not on the spindle centerline. Always return Y to zero before switching back to turning mode. The Y-axis combined with C-axis enables eccentric turning and complex contouring.
gotchas: Y-axis travel is only +/-115mm — not suitable for large milling operations
Y MUST be at zero when switching to turning mode — turning with Y offset will crash
Y-axis rigidity is lower than X/Z — reduce milling feed rates by 20% for Y-axis cuts
Combined Y+B offsets can exceed the effective work envelope — verify clearance in simulation

programming_tips.topic: Polar Interpolation for Face Milling Patterns (G12.1)
programming_tips.code_example:
M19 (C-axis engage)
G00 B90. M68
G97 S4000 M33
G12.1 (Polar interpolation ON)
G01 X20. C0. F300 (Move to R20, angle 0)
G01 C90. (Arc to 90 degrees at R20)
G01 X30. (Radial move out to R30)
G13.1 (Polar interpolation OFF)
programming_tips.description: G12.1 converts the XC coordinate system to polar coordinates where X is the radius and C is the angle in degrees. This enables milling patterns on the face of a turned part (bolt circles, curved slots, spiral grooves). The milling spindle must be at B=90 for face milling. C-axis provides continuous rotation while X provides radial feed. Feed rate in G12.1 mode is along the resulting XC path, not individual axes.
gotchas: X is radius (not diameter) in polar mode
C is degrees, not distance — a C move at large X radius covers more distance than at small radius
F (feed rate) applies to the resultant path — actual axis speeds are calculated by the controller
G12.1 only works with the C-axis — not with the B-axis

programming_tips.code_example:
M19
G00 B90. M68
G97 S6000 M33
G107 C25. (Cylinder radius = 25mm)
G01 X0. C0. Z0. F200
G01 C90. Z-10. (Helical path on cylinder surface)
G107 C0 (Cancel cylindrical interpolation)
programming_tips.description: G107 maps a flat XC toolpath onto a cylindrical surface of the specified radius. The C value in the G107 command defines the cylinder radius. Within G107 mode, C-axis movement is expressed as distance on the cylinder surface (not degrees). This enables engraving, spline milling, and helical feature cutting on turned part ODs and IDs.
gotchas: C-axis values inside G107 are surface DISTANCE in mm, not degrees
The cylinder radius in G107 must match the actual part radius being machined
Feedrate F is surface speed along the cylinder, not axis speed
G107 must be canceled (G107 C0) before returning to standard turning

programming_tips.topic: Sub-Spindle Part Transfer on MULTUS B300II-W
programming_tips.code_example:
(Sync spindle speeds before transfer)
M200 (Spindle sync ON — both spindles match RPM)
G04 P2000 (Allow 2 sec for sync lock)
(Sub-spindle advance to grip part)
G00 W2=2. (Sub-spindle Z2 axis advance)
M210 (Sub-spindle chuck clamp)
G04 P500
M11 (Main chuck open)
G00 W2=-50. (Sub-spindle retract with part)
M201 (Spindle sync OFF)
programming_tips.description: On the dual-spindle MULTUS B300II-W model, part transfer uses synchronized spindle rotation (M200/M201) so the part can be picked up at RPM without stopping. This dramatically reduces cycle time versus stop-transfer methods. The sub-spindle has its own Z2 axis for approach and retract. Chuck clamp/unclamp sequencing must be rigidly ordered to prevent dropped parts.
gotchas: Spindle sync (M200) requires both spindles at same RPM and direction before engaging
G04 dwell after M200 is critical — sync needs 1-2 seconds to stabilize
Sub-spindle MUST confirm clamp before main chuck opens — verify interlock in program
Part-off must be complete before transfer — partial part-off will jam both chucks

programming_tips.code_example:
(TURNING COORDINATE SYSTEM)
(X = diameter, Z = along spindle axis)
(No Y, no B active)

(MILLING COORDINATE SYSTEM — B=90)
(X = radial from spindle center, Y = lateral offset)
(Z = along spindle axis, C = rotation around Z)

(MILLING COORDINATE SYSTEM — B=0)
(X = radial, Z = depth into part face)
(This is boring/end-face milling orientation)
programming_tips.description: The MULTUS B300II uses different coordinate interpretations depending on the operating mode and B-axis angle. In turning mode, X is diameter and there is no Y-axis. In milling mode at B=90, X is the radial distance from spindle center and Y is the lateral offset. At B=0, the milling spindle is parallel to Z (boring orientation). Understanding these coordinate systems is essential for writing correct mill-turn programs.
gotchas: X is DIAMETER in turning mode but RADIUS in some milling interpolation modes (G12.1)
Tool offsets are stored differently for turning tools (geometry X/Z) vs milling tools (length/diameter)
G54-G59 work offsets apply to the currently active coordinate system
Switching modes does not automatically reset work offsets — verify G54 values after mode switch

programming_tips.code_example:
M310 (Anti-collision checkpoint — force recalculation)
(Use M310 at every mode transition and before rapid moves)

(Tool model registration in OSP anti-collision screen:)
(1. Enter tool holder dimensions for each turret station)
(2. Enter milling tool assembly dimensions for each ATC pocket)
(3. Set chuck jaw model to match actual jaw configuration)
(4. Enable collision check: Parameter > Safety > Anti-Collision = ON)
programming_tips.description: The MULTUS B300II has an integrated anti-collision system that models the turret, milling head, chuck, tailstock, and tools in 3D. It checks every commanded motion against the model BEFORE executing. For this to work, all tool holder and tool assembly dimensions must be registered accurately. M310 forces a collision-check recalculation at critical points in the program.
gotchas: Anti-collision ONLY works if tool models are accurately registered — wrong dimensions = false safety
The system adds 10-50ms overhead per block for collision checking
M310 should be placed before every rapid move after a mode switch
Anti-collision does NOT protect against incorrect work offsets — the model assumes offsets are correct

programming_tips.code_example:
G00 B90. C0.
M68 (B-clamp OFF for simultaneous)
M69 (Actually, for 5-axis simultaneous, B must be UNclamped)
G43.4 H1 (TCP ON)
G01 X30. Y0. Z-5. B85. C10. F500
G01 X30. Y5. Z-5. B80. C20. F500
...
G49 (TCP OFF)
M68 (Re-clamp B)
programming_tips.description: For true 5-axis simultaneous milling (X/Y/Z + B + C all moving at once), the B-axis must be unclamped (M69) and TCP (G43.4) must be active. TCP maintains the tool tip at the programmed XYZ position while B and C tilt the tool orientation. Without TCP, the XYZ position would shift as B/C rotate. This mode is used for turbine blade finishing, impeller machining, and complex sculptured surfaces.
gotchas: B-axis MUST be unclamped (M69) for simultaneous 5-axis — clamped B will cause servo alarm
TCP tool length offset must be measured precisely — 0.1mm error at tool tip creates larger error at B-axis lever arm
5-axis simultaneous produces higher servo loads — reduce feed rate by 30-40% compared to 3-axis
Verify the post processor outputs B/C values in the correct convention (Euler angles vs tool vectors)

programming_tips.topic: Spindle Load Monitoring for Tool Wear — Dual Spindle
programming_tips.code_example:
(Main spindle load)
IF [VSPLD GT 85] GOTO 8000

(Milling spindle load)
IF [VMSPLD GT 80] GOTO 8100

N8000 M01 (Main spindle overload)
N8100 M01 (Milling spindle overload)
programming_tips.description: VSPLD reads the main (turning) spindle load percentage. VMSPLD reads the milling spindle load percentage. Monitor both during complex mill-turn cycles. Turning operations typically run at 40-70% spindle load. Milling operations vary more — heavy face milling can reach 80% while finishing stays under 30%.
gotchas: VSPLD and VMSPLD are different variables — use the correct one for the active spindle
Load thresholds must be calibrated per operation — a threshold set for roughing will false-alarm during finishing
During spindle sync (M200), VSPLD reflects combined load of both spindles
